args: sam toPairAlign --help
exit: 0
--- stdout
Convert a SAM file to pairwise alignments in fasta format

Each query is written as a pairwise alignment with the reference: the reference sequence first, then the
query. Unlike toMultiAlign, insertions relative to the reference are kept (unless you use --skip-insertions),
so the output alignment can be longer than the reference. External alignment gaps are always written as N.

--reference must be the fasta file that was used to generate the sam file, and its sequence must be the same
length as the @SQ line in the sam header.

Example usage:
	gofasta sam toPairAlign -s aligned.sam -r reference.fasta -o alignments

writes one file per query to the directory alignments (which is created if it doesn't exist). Each file is
named after its query, with any "/" replaced by "_", plus ".fasta". To write all the alignments to stdout
instead, use -o stdout, e.g.:
	minimap2 -a -x asm20 --score-N=0 reference.fasta unaligned.fasta | gofasta sam toPairAlign -r reference.fasta -o stdout

Usage:
  gofasta sam toPairAlign [flags]

Aliases:
  toPairAlign, topairalign, topa

Flags:
  -o, --outpath string    Directory to write one fasta file per query to, or stdout to write all the alignments to stdout (required)
      --omit-reference    Omit the reference sequences from the output alignments
      --skip-insertions   Skip insertions relative to the reference from the output alignments
      --start int         1-based first nucleotide position (in reference coordinates) to retain in the output. Bases before this position are omitted (default -1)
      --end int           1-based last nucleotide position (in reference coordinates) to retain in the output. Bases after this position are omitted (default -1)
  -w, --wrap int          Wrap the output alignment to this number of nucleotides wide. Omit this option not to wrap the output. (default -1)
      --strict            Stop with an error at the first record that can't be processed, instead of warning and skipping it
  -h, --help              help for toPairAlign

Global Flags:
  -r, --reference string   Reference fasta file used to generate the sam file
  -s, --samfile string     SAM file to read (default "stdin")
  -t, --threads int        Number of threads (and CPUs) to use: 0, the default, for all of them
--- stderr
